subject: Consolidating per-pathline telemetry for cost + latency ownership
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Acme Analytics <ops@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Consolidating per-pathline telemetry for cost + latency ownership

Team / Acme —

Quick ask to align on a single mapping we can use in the Console for per-route cost/latency breakdowns. Acme's engagement (cc'd Claire) surfaced that their product teams want:

- A deterministic mapping from a request "pathline" (their term for a sequence of model calls and webhook steps) to a consistent cost & latency fingerprint we can show in the tenant drill.
- Clear owner metadata so CS and billing know who to loop in when we show a spike.
- Sampling guidance (prefix vs full trace) — they want actionable numbers rather than noisy percentiles.

Proposed immediate outputs:
1) A small CSV with 50 sample traces from Acme (attached) so infra can infer typical token-length distributions.
2) A one-pager that defines "pathline" in our schema and maps it to our existing route/tag model.
3) A Console mock (png attached) showing where the per-pathline row appears and the owner column.

Can Naomi / Marcus / Jasmine weigh in on feasibility and any performance or storage caveats? Acme — are those sample traces sufficient? If yes, I'd like to schedule a 30-min sync early next week to lock scope.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernández
Customer Solutions – Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: per_pathline_trace_sample.csv (CSV, 47KB), console_wireframe_draft.png (PNG, 210KB)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Acme Analytics <ops@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consolidating per-pathline telemetry for cost + latency ownership

Diego — thanks for putting this together, great framing. Quick thoughts: 

- Feasibility: We can produce a per-pathline fingerprint that combines token count distribution + model variant mix + average KV-cache hit rate. The tricky bit is ensuring stable "owner" metadata — that has to come from the customer route tags or from a tenant-side annotation.
- Storage & sampling: I'd recommend a two-tier approach:
  * Full traces for 1 in 5k requests retained for 30 days (for forensic/accuracy checks).
  * Aggregated pathline summaries (histograms + 99/95/50 latencies, token quantiles) for all paths, rolled up hourly and retained 90 days.
- Console UX: The mock looks fine — we should add an expandable row that shows a small heatmap (token vs latency) on hover.

Action items I can own:
1) Draft a minimal schema for the pathline fingerprint by EOD Monday.
2) Work with infra (Marcus) on estimated storage/ingest cost numbers.

Marcus — can you call out any GPU/ingest implications for the two-tier sampling? Jasmine — can you validate this UX fits within the current Console constraints?

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@acme-analytics.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 12:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Consolidating per-pathline telemetry for cost + latency ownership

On Fri, May 25, 2028 at 9:14 AM Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team / Acme —
> 
> Quick ask to align on a single mapping we can use in the Console for per-route cost/latency breakdowns.

Thanks Diego — this is exactly what we've been asking for. The attached CSV is a small extract from our staging logs (we redacted user ids) — it includes the pathline id, sequence of model calls, total token counts, and per-hop durations.

A few clarifying points from our side:
- Ownership: we can push a tenant-level annotation header (x-acme-path-owner) so each request includes an owner handle. That should avoid manual mapping on Redwood's side.
- Sampling: 1-in-5k full traces sounds OK for now; we can increase sampling if we detect a spike.
- Rollout: can we have the per-pathline view in Console visible to any user with "billing_read" scope, and a separate button for exporting raw pathline CSVs to users with "billing_admin"?

Happy to join a 30-min kickoff — I'm available Mon 5/28 10–11am PT or Tue 5/29 8–10am PT.

Claire Zhou
Platform Engineer, Acme Analytics
Acme Analytics
